claim: During human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) infection lymphoid organ follicular dendritic cells (FDCs) serve as a reservoir for infectious virus and an obstacle to curative therapies.
source: During human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) infection lymphoid organ follicular dendritic cells (FDCs) serve as a reservoir for infectious virus and an obstacle to curative therapies.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established knowledge about HIV-1 infection and FDCs.

claim: A subset of lymphoid organ sinus lining macrophages (SMs) provide a cell-cell contact portal that facilitates the uptake of HIV-1 viral-like particles (VLPs) by FDCs and B cells in mouse lymph node.
source: Here, we identify a subset of lymphoid organ sinus lining macrophage (SMs) that provide a cell-cell contact portal, which facilitates the uptake of HIV-1 viral-like particles (VLPs) by FDCs and B cells in mouse lymph node.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The bridging glycoprotein MFG-E8 is central for portal function.
source: Central for portal function is the bridging glycoprotein MFG-E8.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data showing MFG-E8's role in VLP transfer.

claim: MFG-E8 uses a phosphatidylserine binding domain and an RGD motif to help target HIV-1 VLPs to αv integrin bearing SMs.
source: Using a phosphatidylserine binding domain and an RGD motif, MFG-E8 helps target HIV-1 VLPs to αv integrin bearing SMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data showing MFG-E8 binding to VLPs and integrins.

claim: Lack of MFG-E8 or integrin blockade severely limits HIV-1 VLP spread onto FDC networks.
source: Lack of MFG-E8 or integrin blockade severely limits HIV-1 VLP spread onto FDC networks.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data from MFG-E8 knockout mice and integrin blocking experiments.

claim: Direct SM-FDC virion transfer depends upon short-lived FDC network abutment, likely triggered by SCSM antigen uptake.
source: Direct SM-FDC virion transfer also depends upon short-lived FDC network abutment, likely triggered by SCSM antigen uptake.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by intravital imaging data showing FDC movement toward SCSMs.

claim: Locally injected ultraviolet-light inactivated vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) rapidly appeared in the lymph and accumulated at discrete sites on SCSMs.
source: For example, locally injected ultraviolet-light inactivated vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) rapidly appeared in the lymph and accumulated at discrete sites on SCSMs.
evidence: This statement references prior work on VSV uptake by SCSMs.

claim: VSV capture and accumulation on the SCSM did not depend upon natural antibody and complement C3 fixation.
source: While the mechanism responsible for VSV capture and accumulation on the SCSM was not identified, it did not depend upon natural antibody and complement C3 fixation as no defect in SCSM VSV retention occurred in animals that lacked C3.
evidence: This statement references prior experimental findings about VSV capture mechanisms.

claim: SCSMs retained locally injected adenovirus, vaccinia virus, HIV-1, and murine leukemia virus like particles (VLPs).
source: Furthermore, the capture mechanism was not unique to VSV as SCSMs also retained locally injected adenovirus and vaccinia virus as well as HIV-1 and murine leukemia virus like particles (VLPs) (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Junt et al., 2007 on SCSM capture of various viruses.

claim: Antibodies directed against CD169 reduced VLP capture by SCSMs.
source: Implicating the SCSM scavenger receptor CD169/sialoadhesin in HIV-1 and MLV-VLPs uptake, antibodies directed against CD169 reduced VLP capture.
evidence: This statement references prior experimental findings about CD169's role in VLP capture.

claim: CD169 target sialyllactose is found on gangliosides embedded in the HIV-1 and MLV lipid membranes.
source: A known CD169 target sialyllactose is found on gangliosides embedded in the HIV-1 and MLV lipid membranes (Sewald et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Sewald et al., 2015 on CD169 binding targets.

claim: SCSM likely employ multiple other receptors to capture material flowing in the lymph besides CD169.
source: Besides CD169 SCSM likely employ multiple other receptors to capture material flowing in the lymph (Gray and Cyster, 2012).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Gray and Cyster, 2012 and represents an inference about SCSM receptor diversity.

claim: VSV rapidly translocates along the SCSM membrane penetrating the SCS floor after binding to an SCSM.
source: Once bound to an SCSM, a virus such as VSV rapidly translocate along the SCSM membrane penetrating the SCS floor.
evidence: This statement references prior observations about VSV behavior on SCSMs.

claim: SCSM membrane processes bearing virus project into the underlying B cell follicle, allowing migrating virus-specific B cells access to the viral particles.
source: SCSM membrane processes bearing virus project into the underlying B cell follicle. This allows migrating virus-specific B cells access to the viral particles.
evidence: This statement references prior observations about SCSM-B cell interactions.

claim: SCSM macrophage depletion in VSV infection compromised viral retention, worsened viremia, and impaired B cell responses.
source: In VSV infection, SCSM macrophage depletion compromised viral retention, worsened viremia, and impaired B cell responses (Junt et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement references prior experimental findings by Junt et al., 2007 on the consequences of SCSM depletion.

claim: Captured murine leukemia virus VLPs translocated along the SCSM membrane becoming available to B1 B cells, a target of MLV infection.
source: Somewhat analogously, captured murine leukemia virus VLPs translocated along the SCSM membrane becoming available to B1 B cells, a target of MLV infection.
evidence: This statement references prior observations about MLV-VLP behavior on SCSMs.

claim: Once infected with MLV, B1 cells migrated to other lymph nodes to spread the infection.
source: Once infected the B1 cells migrated to other lymph nodes to spread the infection (Sewald et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement references prior findings by Sewald et al., 2015 on MLV infection spread.

claim: FDCs are critical for humoral immunity as they serve as a long-term repository for unprocessed antigens and form a framework for the germinal center and B cell memory responses.
source: FDCs are critical for humoral immunity as they serve as a long-term repository for unprocessed antigens and form a framework for the germinal center and B cell memory responses (Mandels et al., 1980).
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about FDC function, citing Mandels et al., 1980.

claim: The ability of FDCs to retain HIV-1 virion for prolonged durations poses a significant challenge to the eradication of HIV-1 infection in patients.
source: In patients infected with HIV-1 the ability of FDCs to retain HIV-1 virion for prolonged durations poses a significant challenge to the eradication of the infection.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about HIV-1 persistence on FDCs.

claim: The FDC HIV-1-reservoir contributes to low level viremia.
source: The FDC HIV-1-reservoir contributes to low level viremia.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about the FDC reservoir's contribution to viremia.

claim: The FDC HIV-1 reservoir provides a potential source of infectious virus for the viral resurgence that typically occurs following treatment interruption.
source: It also provides a potential source of infectious virus for the viral resurgence that typically occurs following treatment interruption (Heath et al., 1995; Schacker et al., 2000; Smith et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement references prior work on HIV-1 viral rebound after treatment interruption, citing Heath et al., 1995; Schacker et al., 2000; Smith et al., 2001.

claim: Complement receptor 2 (CR2, CD21) is important for FDC retention of virions.
source: Important for FDC retention of virions is the complement receptor 2 (CR2, CD21).
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about CR2's role in FDC function.

claim: FDCs prominently express CR2, which binds the complement components C3d and iC3b.
source: FDCs prominently express CR2, which binds the complement components C3d and iC3b.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about CR2 expression and binding specificity on FDCs.

claim: FDCs express CR1 (CD35), which binds C3b, iC3b, C4b, and iC4b.
source: FDCs also express a related protein termed CR1 (CD35), which binds C3b, iC3b, C4b, and iC4b (Carroll, 1998).
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about CR1 expression and binding specificity on FDCs, citing Carroll, 1998.

claim: Virions become associated with complement components due to their recognition by natural and specific antibodies that fix complement.
source: Virions become associated with complement components due to their recognition by natural and specific antibodies that fix complement.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about immune complex formation.

claim: FDC complement receptors retain HIV-1 virions as immune complexes (IC) on lymphoid organ FDC networks.
source: This allows FDC complement receptors to retain the HIV-1 virions as immune complexes (IC) on lymphoid organ FDC networks (Armstrong, 1984).
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about FDC retention of immune complexes, citing Armstrong, 1984.

claim: Antibodies that recognize CD21/CD35 are used to identify FDCs in tissue sections.
source: Antibodies that recognize CD21/CD35 are used to identify FDCs in tissue sections.
evidence: This statement references established methodology for identifying FDCs.

claim: Follicular B cells can be distinguished from FDCs based on their morphology and lower CR2 expression level.
source: While follicular B cells also express CR2, they can be distinguished from FDCs based on their morphology and lower CR2 expression level.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about distinguishing FDCs from B cells.

claim: FDC-M1 antibody is used to recognize FDCs in tissue sections.
source: Another marker used to recognize FDCs in tissue sections is FDC-M1 (Haley et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement references established methodology for identifying FDCs, citing Haley et al., 1995.

claim: The FDC-M1 antibody binds MFG-E8, a bridging molecule that possesses a phosphatidylserine (PS) binding domain and a second domain that contains an RGD motif.
source: The FDC-M1 antibody binds MFG-E8, a bridging molecule that possesses a phosphatidylserine (PS) binding domain and a second domain that contains an RGD motif (Kranich et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Kranich et al., 2008 on FDC-M1 antibody specificity.

claim: Human and mouse MFG-E8 have two PS binding domains termed C1 and C2.
source: Human and mouse MFG-E8 have two PS binding domains termed C1 and C2.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about MFG-E8 structure.

claim: Human MFG-E8 has a single RGD motif binding domain while the mouse has a short and an extended version, which possesses a solitary, or two RGD motif binding domains, respectively.
source: Human MFG-E8 has a single RGD motif binding domain while the mouse has a short and an extended version, which possesses a solitary, or two RGD motif binding domains, respectively (Hanayama et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Hanayama et al., 2002 on MFG-E8 structure.

claim: In lymphoid organs, MFG-E8 binds PS bearing apoptotic cells delivering them to αvβ3 integrin bearing tingible body macrophages (TBM).
source: In lymphoid organs, MFG-E8 binds PS bearing apoptotic cells delivering them to αvβ3 integrin bearing tingible body macrophages (TBM).
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about MFG-E8 function in apoptotic cell clearance.

claim: Engagement of αvβ3 integrins promotes the phagocytosis and eventual destruction of the apoptotic cell by the macrophages.
source: Engagement of αvβ3 integrins promotes the phagocytosis and eventual destruction of the apoptotic cell by the macrophages (Asano et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Asano et al., 2004 on integrin-mediated phagocytosis.

claim: MFG-E8 and related proteins can bind PS present in viral envelopes.
source: Besides, binding apoptotic cells, MFG-E8 and related proteins can bind PS present in viral envelopes (Morizono and Chen, 2014).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Morizono and Chen, 2014 on MFG-E8 binding to viral envelopes.

claim: As HIV-1 viral particles bud from the host cell, the viral envelope can selectively acquire proteins and lipids from host membranes.
source: As HIV-1 viral particles bud from the host cell, the viral envelope can selectively acquire proteins and lipids from host membranes.
evidence: This statement references established knowledge about HIV-1 viral budding.

claim: During viral budding the PS becomes exposed on the HIV-1 envelope potentially serving as a target for MFG-E8 and related PS binding proteins.
source: While PS is normally located on the plasma membrane inner leaflet during viral budding the PS becomes exposed on the HIV-1 envelope potentially serving as a target for MFG-E8 and related PS binding proteins (Morizono and Chen, 2014; Wu and Shroff, 2018).
evidence: This statement references prior work by Morizono and Chen, 2014; Wu and Shroff, 2018 on PS exposure on HIV-1 envelopes.

claim: MFG-E8 is widely expressed and found at substantial concentrations in blood and potentially the lymph.
source: Because MFG-E8 is widely expressed and found at substantial concentrations in blood and potentially the lymph (Kishi et al., 2017; Yamaguchi et al., 2008); most HIV-1 virions likely bear MFG-E8.
evidence: This statement references prior work by Kishi et al., 2017; Yamaguchi et al., 2008 on MFG-E8 expression and distribution.

claim: Most HIV-1 virions likely bear MFG-E8.
source: Because MFG-E8 is widely expressed and found at substantial concentrations in blood and potentially the lymph (Kishi et al., 2017; Yamaguchi et al., 2008); most HIV-1 virions likely bear MFG-E8.
evidence: This is an inference based on MFG-E8 abundance and its ability to bind PS on viral envelopes.

claim: MFG-E8 bound to HIV-1 virions would target them to monocytes and macrophages that express αvβ3/5 integrins.
source: This would target HIV-1 virions to monocytes and macrophages that express αvβ3/5 integrins.
evidence: This is an inference based on MFG-E8's known binding to αvβ3/5 integrins.

claim: MFG-E8 binding to HIV-1 virions would provide another mechanism in addition to CD169 for SCSMs to capture HIV-1 virions from the lymph.
source: This would also provide another mechanism in addition to CD169 for SCSMs to capture HIV-1 virions from the lymph.
evidence: This is an inference based on MFG-E8's ability to bind both virions and integrins on SCSMs.

claim: HIV-1 VLPs (NL4.3-GFP) rapidly localized (1 hr) on the SCSMs that overlie the LN follicle rather than those over the interfollicular region.
source: Suggesting that gp120 does not direct HIV-1 virion uptake, the HIV-1 VLPs (NL4.3-GFP) rapidly localized (1 hr) on the SCSMs that overlie the LN follicle rather than those over the interfollicular region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: At 6 hr post injection some of the HIV-1 VLPs had moved inside the lymph node consistent with early FDC loading.
source: At the 6 hr time point some of the VLPs had moved inside the lymph node consistent with early FDC loading (Figure 1A and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: By 20 hr post injection many of the HIV-1 VLPs had transited deep into the B cell follicle, consistent with extensive FDC loading.
source: By 20 hr post injection many of the VLPs had transited deep into the B cell follicle, consistent with extensive FDC loading (Figure 1B and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 1B and Video 1.

claim: Both HIV-1 and MLV VLP sets appeared on overlapping sites on the SCSMs (~88% colocalization index).
source: Following injection of the VLPs, both VLP sets appeared on overlapping sites on the SCSMs (~88% colocalization index, Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Both HIV-1 and MLV VLPs localized on lymph node FDCs that had directly contacted the overlying SCSMs.
source: We also noted that both sets of VLPs localized on lymph node FDCs that had directly contacted the overlying SCSMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data.

claim: SCSM-FDC contacts persisted as they were readily observed at 8 hr post injection.
source: These contacts persisted as they were readily observed at 8 hr post injection (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The FDC-M1 antibody precisely delineated the SCSM membrane sites where the VLPs had localized.
source: Surprisingly, we found that besides identifying the lymph node FDCs, the FDC-M1 antibody precisely delineated the SCSM membrane sites where the VLPs had localized (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The FDC-M1 immunostaining often encased the VLPs, and when not confluent appeared vesicular.
source: The FDC-M1 immunostaining often encased the VLPs, and when not confluent appeared vesicular.
evidence: This is a primary observation from confocal microscopy data.

claim: FDC-M1 SCSM defined sites extended into the underlying follicle directly abutting FDCs processes.
source: These FDC-M1 SCSM defined sites extended into the underlying follicle directly abutting FDCs processes.
evidence: This is a primary observation from confocal microscopy data.

claim: Intensity mapping shows strong overlap between MFG-E8 and the two VLPs on SCSMs.
source: Intensity mapping of the three signals on SCSMs shows the strong overlap between MFG-E8 and the two VLPs (Figure 1F, far right).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intensity mapping analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The CD169+ macrophages captured most of the NL4.3-GFP+ signal.
source: The CD169+ macrophages captured most of the NL4.3-GFP+ signal (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: When CD169+ macrophages were separated based on MFG-E8 expression, the MFG-E8 high subset bound the most NL4.3-GFP.
source: and when separated based on MFG-E8 expression, the MFG-E8 high subset bound the most (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: Blood-borne HIV-1 VLPs were captured by marginal zone macrophages and transferred to the splenic white pulp FDC networks.
source: After 6 hr we collected the spleens of the injected animals and made thick splenic sections for immunohistochemistry (Figure 1H). We found a similar scenario as we had noted in the lymph nodes, the accumulation of HIV-1 VLPs on marginal zone macrophages at MFG-E8 rich sites and the appearance of VLPs on the underlying FDC networks.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Sinus lining macrophages in contact with the blood or the lymph collect HIV-1 VLPs at sites on the macrophages enriched for MFG-E8.
source: Thus, sinus lining macrophages in contact with the blood or the lymph collect HIV-1 VLPs at sites on the macrophages enriched for MFG-E8.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on both lymph node and splenic macrophages.

claim: MFG-E8 encases HIV-1 VLPs as shown by STED microscopy.
source: To determine whether MFG-E8 can bind the HIV-1 VLPs, we used stimulated emission depletion (STED) microscopy to examine NL4.3-GFP VLPs incubated with directly labeled recombinant MFG-E8. The images show MFG-E8 encasing the VLPs (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by STED microscopy data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–F.

claim: MFG-E8 bound PS, but not phosphatidylcholine (PC) liposomes.
source: As expected MFG-E8 bound PS, but not phosphatidylcholine (PC) liposomes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by STED microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The addition of recombinant MFG-E8 to the VLPs resulted in a strong shift in the intensity of the MFG-E8 antibody staining (~90% of VLPs were MFG-E8+).
source: However, the addition of recombinant MFG-E8 to the VLPs resulted in a strong shift in the intensity of the MFG-E8 antibody staining (~90% of VLPs were MFG-E8+) (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Directly labeled recombinant MFG-E8 bound HIV-1 VLPs in a dose dependent manner.
source: and directly labeled recombinant MFG-E8 bound HIV-1 VLPs in a dose dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: PS containing, but not PC liposomes competed for the VLP MFG-E8 binding.
source: PS containing, but not PC liposomes competed for the VLP MFG-E8 binding (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Locally injected PS enriched liposomes exhibited an SCSM uptake pattern much like NL4.3-GFP, while inter-follicular and medullary SMs predominately gathered injected PC liposomes.
source: When we injected mice with labeled PS enriched liposomes the lymph node exhibited an SCSM uptake pattern much like NL4.3-GFP, while inter-follicular and medullary SMs predominately gathered injected PC liposomes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Adding recombinant αvβ3 integrins allowed detection of αvβ3/MFG-E8/NL4.3-GFP complexes.
source: Adding recombinant αvβ3 integrins allowed detection of αvβ3/MFG-E8/NL4.3-GFP complexes (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The addition of recombinant MFG-E8 to the VLPs resulted in a strong binding to the αvβ3 integrins (~80% of VLPs were αvβ3/MFG-E8 positive).
source: The addition of recombinant MFG-E8 to the VLPs resulted in a strong binding to the αvβ3 integrins (~80% of VLPs were αvβ3/MFG-E8 positive) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: MFG-E8 bound VLPs likely bind to integrin αvβ3 on SCSM.
source: Together these results indicate that MFG-E8 bound VLPs likely bind to integrin αvβ3 on SCSM.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on MFG-E8 and integrin binding.

claim: Immunostaining lymph node sections with an αv (CD51) antibody visualized αvβ3/5 integrins co-localized with the NL4.3-GFP VLPs in the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment.
source: Immunostaining the sections with an αv (CD51) antibody visualized αvβ3/5 integrins co-localized with the NL4.3-GFP VLPs in the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Colocalization analysis showed that approximately 85% of NL4.3-GFP colocalized on αv integrin.
source: Colocalization analysis showed that approximately 85% of NL4.3-GFP colocalized on αv integrin (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The injected VLPs acquire endogenous MFG-E8, which promotes their capture by SCSMs bearing αvβ3 integrins.
source: These data indicate that the injected VLPs acquire endogenous MFG-E8, which promotes their capture by SCSMs bearing αvβ3 integrins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on VLP localization with MFG-E8 and integrins.

claim: Human peripheral blood monocytes expressed αvβ3 integrins, while CD4 and CD8 T cells did not.
source: As expected, human peripheral blood monocytes expressed αvβ3 integrins, while CD4 and CD8 T cells did not (Figure 3C), nor did peripheral blood B cells (data not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The addition of MFG-E8 resulted in a substantial increase in NL4.3-GFP binding to human monocytes as approximately 25% of the cells had both an MFG-E8 and a VLP signal.
source: however, the addition of MFG-E8 resulted in a substantial increase in NL4.3-GFP binding as approximately 25% of the cells had both an MFG-E8 and a VLP signal (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: PS containing liposomes, but not PC liposomes competitively inhibited the MFG-E8/VLP binding to human monocytes.
source: PS containing liposomes, but not PC liposomes competitively inhibited the MFG-E8/VLP binding (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: MFG-E8 bound HIV-1 virions likely target human peripheral blood monocytes by binding to αvβ3 integrins.
source: Thus, MFG-E8 bound HIV-1 virions likely target human peripheral blood monocytes by binding to αvβ3 integrins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on MFG-E8-mediated VLP binding to human monocytes.

claim: Double blockade (RGDyK + αCD51) strongly reduced SSCM NL4.3-GFP uptake.
source: however double blockade (RGDyK + αCD51) strongly reduced SSCM uptake (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The double blockade partially inhibited the initial NL4.3-mCherry binding (below 10 μm) and strongly inhibited the later binding (top 10 μm).
source: The double blockade partially inhibited the initial NL4.3-mCherry binding (below 10 μm) and strongly inhibited the later binding (top 10 μm), (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The integrin blockade strongly reduced FDC loading.
source: Furthermore, the integrin blockade strongly reduced FDC loading (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The integrin blockade shifted the VLP targeting to the medullary SMs.
source: and shifted the VLP targeting to the medullary SMs (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and Figure 4—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: The integrin blockade displaced those NL4.3-GFP VLPs captured from the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment.
source: Of note, the integrin blockade displaced those NL4.3-GFP VLPs captured from the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment (Figure 4B, right panels).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The double blockade reduced the MFG-E8 localized on SCSMs and decreased the FDC-SCSM contacts.
source: Additionally, the double blockade reduced the MFG-E8 localized on SCSMs and decreased the FDC-SCSM contacts (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: The injected NL4.3-GFP still accumulated on the Mfg-e8-/- SCSMs at 20 hr post injection.
source: In contrast to our expectation, the injected NL4.3-GFP still accumulated on the Mfg-e8-/- SCSMs at 20 hr post injection.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments using MFG-E8 deficient mice.

claim: The MFG-E8 deficiency markedly impaired FDC NL4.3-GFP loading.
source: Yet, the MFG-E8 deficiency markedly impaired FDC NL4.3-GFP loading (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Mfg-e8-/- SCSMs accumulated more VLPs than did the controls, possibly due to poor FDC delivery.
source: Perhaps due to the poor FDC delivery, the Mfg-e8-/- SCSMs accumulated more VLPs than did the controls (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantification shown in Figure 4D, with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Injecting recombinant MFG-E8 along with NL4.3-GFP into Mfg-e8-/- mice partially reconstituted the MFG-E8 high compartment on the SCSMs and helped transfer some of the VLPs to the FDC network.
source: Injecting recombinant MFG-E8 along with NL4.3-GFP into Mfg-e8-/- mice partially reconstituted the MFG-E8 high compartment on the SCSMs and helped transfer some of the VLPs to the FDC network (Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 6.

claim: SCSM αvβ3/5 integrins can shuttle MFG-E8 bound material to the MFG-E8+ compartment.
source: Together this data suggests that SCSM αvβ3/5 integrins can shuttle MFG-E8 bound material to the MFG-E8+ compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the integrin blockade and MFG-E8 deficiency experiments.

claim: The MFG-E8+ compartment is open to lymph node FDCs and B cells.
source: This compartment is open to lymph node FDCs and B cells (see below).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on VLP transfer to FDCs and B cells.

claim: SCSMs that lack functional αv integrins to bind MFG-E8/NL4.3-GFP complexes cannot load the MFG-E8+ compartment or FDCs.
source: SCSMs that lack functional αv integrins to bind MFG-E8/NL4.3-GFP complexes cannot load the MFG-E8+ compartment or FDCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the integrin blockade experiments.

claim: The majority of the VLPs in the HEK293T cell culture had bound the VRC01 antibody.
source: In contrast to negative controls, we found that the majority of the VLPs in the cell culture had bound the VRC01 antibody (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A & B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A & B.

claim: Many of the NL4.3-GFPs bound the MFG-E8 antibody indicating that had sufficient bound MFG-E8 to allow their detection.
source: Again, many of the NL4.3-GFPs bound the MFG-E8 antibody indicating that had sufficient bound MFG-E8 to allow their detection (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and Video 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1E and Video 4.

claim: Adding a 1:1 molar ratio of EDIL-3 to MFG-E8 reduced MFG-E8 binding to human monocytes by approximately 50%.
source: Adding a 1:1 molar ratio of EDIL-3 to MFG-E8 reduced MFG-E8 binding to human monocytes by approximately 50% (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1F.

claim: HIV-1 virions are likely bound not only by MFG-E8 but also by other PS binding proteins such as EDIL-3.
source: These results suggest that HIV-1 virions are likely bound not only by MFG-E8 but also by other PS binding proteins such as EDIL-3.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EDIL-3 competition experiments.

claim: There was a strong overlap between the NL4.3-GFP and ICPE SCSM acquisition sites.
source: Surprisingly, we found a strong overlap between the NL4.3-GFP and ICPE SCSM acquisition sites (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Intravital imaging the FDC network beginning 45 min after injection of ICPE showed a dynamic FDC network shift towards SCSMs.
source: Intravital imaging the FDC network beginning 45 min after injection of ICPE showed a dynamic FDC network shift towards SCSMs (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1, and Video 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1, and Video 5.

claim: The intravital imaging revealed direct contact between SCSM bearing ICPE (or HIV-1 VLPs) and FDCs.
source: The intravital imaging revealed direct contact between SCSM bearing ICPE (or HIV-1 VLPs) and FDCs (Figure 6C and Video 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 6C and Video 6.

claim: Pertussis toxin injection 2 hr before NL4.3-GFP VLPs prevented the FDC network from shifting toward the SSCMs and prevented VLPs from accumulating on the FDCs.
source: Examining lymph node sections prepared 6 hr later revealed that SCSM had collected the NL4.3-GFP VLPs, but the FDC network had not shifted toward the SSCMs nor had VLPs accumulated on the FDCs (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: FDCs and adaptively transferred B cells motility was abolished about 1 hr after PTx treatment.
source: FDCs and adaptively transferred B cells motility was abolished about 1 hr after PTx treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding from intravital imaging experiments with pertussis toxin.

claim: An established abutment of SCSM/FDC by ICPE injection started to dissociate about 2 hr after PTx treatment.
source: An established abutment of SCSM/FDC by ICPE injection started to dissociate about 2 hr after PTx treatment.
evidence: This is a primary finding from intravital imaging experiments with pertussis toxin.

claim: The antigen established transient abutments of FDCs and SCSMs are temporal and controlled by Gαi signaling.
source: These results demonstrate that the antigen established transient abutments of FDCs and SCSMs are temporal and controlled by Gαi signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the pertussis toxin experiments.

claim: The transgenic b12 B cells localized at the B-T border, along the inter-follicular channel, and near the SCSMs.
source: Lymph node section prepared 3 hr after VLP injection revealed that the transgenic B cells localized at the B-T border, along the inter-follicular channel, and near the SCSMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding from experiments with gp120-specific b12 B cells.

claim: The transferred wild type B cells tended more towards the center of the follicle, showing little sustained interest in the VLP bearing SCSMs.
source: In contrast, the transferred wild type B cells tended more towards the center of the follicle, showing little sustained interest in the VLP bearing SCSMs (Figure 7A and Video 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7A and Video 8.

claim: Intravital imaging showed b12 B cells extending filopodia to actively probe the NL4.3-GFP bearing SCSMs.
source: Intravital imaging showed b12 B cells extending filopodia to actively probe the NL4.3-GFP bearing SCSMs.
evidence: This is a primary finding from intravital imaging experiments.

claim: Following VLP contact, the b12 B cells reverse direction pulling the VLP now localized on its uropod.
source: Following VLP contact, the B cells reverse direction pulling the VLP now localized on its uropod (Video 9)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Video 9.

claim: Reconstruction of the imaging data shows a b12 B cell extending a filopodium to directly contact an MFG-E8+ SCSM bearing NL4.3-GFP VLPs.
source: Reconstruction of the imaging data shows a b12 B cell extending a filopodium to directly contact an MFG-E8+ SCSM bearing NL4.3-GFP VLPs (Figure 7C and Video 10).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by 3D reconstruction shown in Figure 7C and Video 10.

claim: The b12 B cells were attracted to, and in contact with NL4.3-GFP bearing SCSMs, while wild type B cells failed to develop sustained interactions.
source: Intravital imaging results indicated that the b12 B cells were attracted to, and in contact with NL4.3-GFP bearing SCSMs, while wild type B cells failed to develop sustained interactions (Figure 7E and Video 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by intravital imaging data shown in Figure 7E and Video 8.

claim: The b12 B cells had a reduced mean speed, and turned more frequently (moved less straight) compared to WT B cells.
source: Although the WT and b12 B cell tracks did not have significantly different displacements, the b12 B cells had a reduced mean speed, and turned more frequently (moved less straight).
evidence: This is a primary finding from analysis of B cell tracks in intravital imaging data.

claim: The b12 B cell interacted with the VLP bearing SCSMs for significantly longer times than did the WT B cells.
source: When we focused on those tracks that contacted SCSMs we found that the b12 B cell interacted with the VLP bearing SCSMs for significantly longer times than did the WT B cells (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantification shown in Figure 7F.

claim: B cells with antigen reactive receptors can use the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment to retrieve viruses.
source: These results demonstrate that B cells with antigen reactive receptors can use the SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment to retrieve viruses.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the b12 B cell experiments.

claim: An αvβ3 integrin/MFG-E8 shuttle transfers lymph born HIV-1 from SCSM onto FDCs.
source: Based on our observations, we propose that MFG-E8 blood levels and lymphoid organ sources of MFG-E8 ensure that most cell-free HIV-1 virus in infected individuals is exposed to MFG-E8. HIV-1 envelope PS provides a means for MFG-E8 binding and MFG-E8 links the virions to αv integrins on host cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The SCSM MFG-E8+ compartment functions as a general antigen transfer portal for B cells and the underlying FDCs.
source: Furthermore, we suggest that the SCSM MFG-E8 enriched compartment functions as a general antigen transfer portal for B cells and the underlying FDCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on both VLP and immune complex transfer.

claim: FDCs dynamically react to the delivery of antigen to the overlying SCSMs.
source: In this paradigm FDCs dynamically react to the delivery of antigen to the overlying SCSMs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the intravital imaging data showing FDC movement.
